newsitem.title: CHINA: China belatedly becomes world's top steelmaker.
newsitem.headline: China belatedly becomes world's top steelmaker.

text.p: China's dream of becoming the world's biggest steel maker has come true, albeit 38 years after its leap to achieve that goal created a man-made famine in which at least 28 million people starved to death.
China's steel production broke the 100 million tonne mark in late December, making China the number one steelmaker in the world, the official Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.
"One-hundred million tonnes of steel is the dream of generations of people," Xinhua said.

The dream turned into a nightmare in 1958 when Mao Zedong launched the Great Leap Forward campaign and sponsored "backyard furnaces" all over the country in a bid to surpass Britain's steel output at the time.

Chinese farmers abandoned their fields and joined the mad rush to make steel at Mao's behest, but China was forced to abandon the disastrous programme a year later after harvests failed and millions people died of starvation.
Xinhua trumpeted China's boosting of steel output to 100 million tonnes in just seven years as "rare" in world history.
China produced 60 million tonnes of steel in 1989 and 30 million tonnes in 1978.
China's 24 largest steelmakers each produce more than one million tonnes annually, accounting for 70 percent of total domestic output, Xinhua said.
Minister of Metallurgical Industry Liu Qi said China's domestic manufacturers supplied 88 percent of its steel needs.
